c.tagline: Sumatra's gritty, food-obsessed gateway to Lake Toba.

taxi.fareNote: Blue Bird is the trusted metered taxi brand; insist on the meter or use Gojek/Grab for fixed up-front pricing and to avoid airport touts.

emergency.note: 112 is the general nationwide emergency line; 110 reaches police and 113 the fire service.

avoid.reason: Traffic chaos and petty crime; caution at night

hood_desc: Medan's historic colonial heart along Jalan Ahmad Yani, lined with Dutch-era shophouses, the ornate Tjong A Fie Mansion, and Merdeka Walk's open-air dining; the most central, walkable base for first-timers.
The modern commercial core around Lapangan Merdeka and Sun Plaza, packed with malls, chain hotels, and restaurants; a convenient, well-connected place to stay near the city's main sights.
A leafy, upscale residential district on the site of Medan's former airport, quieter and greener than downtown with mid-range hotels and easy access to the center; good for a calmer stay.
A busy shopping and street-food district anchored by the sprawling Pasar Petisah market, famous for textiles, snacks, and bargain finds; suits travelers who want to eat and shop like a local.
Medan's colourful Little India around the Sri Mariamman Temple, full of Tamil eateries, spice shops, and Hindu temples; an atmospheric, local quarter for cheap food and cultural wandering.
lodging: POP! Hotel Sun Yat Sen Medan

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water only; tap water is not potable.

transit.hours: Trans Metro Deli BRT buses run roughly 5:30 AM to 8:00 PM; angkot (sudako) shared minivans run from early morning until evening. No metro or tram, so ride-hailing fills the late-night gap.
transit.note: Medan has no rail-based city transit. The backbone is the government-run Trans Metro Deli BRT-style bus network, supplemented by the ubiquitous angkot (sudako) shared minivans and app-based ride-hailing.
transit.pay: Trans Metro Deli fares are low and paid on board; angkot fares (a few thousand rupiah) are paid in cash to the driver. There is no citywide smartcard, so carry small notes.

bus: Intercity buses from Amplas and Pinang Baris terminals
ferry: Belawan seaport (regional and cargo services north of the city)
train: Intercity trains from Medan Station to Tebing Tinggi, Pematang Siantar, and Rantau Prapat

transit.m: Railink Airport Rail Link train to Medan City Railway Station (~40-55 min, hourly)
ALS/Damri airport bus to city terminals (~60-90 min)
Metered taxi to city center (45-60 min)

tip.r: Not expected; many restaurants add a 5-10% service charge. Rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated.
